notes:
Summary: Early-stage devtool building a VSCode-embedded code assistant. Inbound via blog + twitter thread. Small engineering team (14) looking to integrate hosted API for self-serve flow. Key asks: long context (20k-32k tokens) for whole-file reviews, predictable per-user rate limits, cheap per-token for real-time completions, and official SDKs for JS + Go in addition to Python.

Details / verbatim: 
- 'We need the assistant to ingest entire repo files and keep context across edits' — Alex (CTO) on 2026-02-20 call.
- Concerned about throttling: dev pilots expect many small requests from editor plugins; want ability to set per-API-key QPS and burst policy.
- Wants streaming responses + delta updates to support low-latency typing UX.
- Interested in prefix/KV caching to avoid re-sending large file context on every keystroke.
- Legal: asked about data retention and whether snippets are persisted; requires SOC2 + audit logs.
- Budget: SMB, annual purchase unlikely now — will likely stay pay-as-you-go but might commit to monthly reserved if pricing aligns.
- Trial ask: provide ~100k token trial credit and temporary uplift on rate limits to run 2-hour stress test (editor load).

Integration notes: 
- Preferred SDKs: npm + go + pypi; want example for streaming with incremental delta tokens and reconnect logic.
- Model footprint: prefer open models but flexible; care more about latency and cost than strictly model brand.
- Metric targets: RT typing latency <150ms per token for short turn completions, average end-to-end completion latency <600ms for 32k context reduce ops. Throughput: 20 concurrent active editors in early beta.

Sales/ops hints: 
- Low churn risk if we can meet latency and onboarding friction low.
- Quote from Alex: 'We won't tolerate lots of manual infra — hosted API only for now.'
